title.value: Scalable Operator Allocation for Multi-Robot Assistance: A Restless Bandit Approach
title.justification: This value was chosen as it reflects the main subject being discussed in the paper: allocating human operators in a system with multiple semi-autonomous robots using a restless bandit framework.
title.quote: Scalable Operator Allocation for Multi-Robot Assistance: A Restless Bandit Approach

extractions.description: This paper addresses the problem of allocating human operators to provide assistance to semi-autonomous robots, which perform tasks but may sometimes get stuck and need human intervention. It introduces an approach using a Restless Bandit formulation to derive scalable index-based policies for operator allocation. This methodology is validated through numerical simulations, demonstrating it outperforms existing scalable approaches.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on optimization techniques for operator allocation in multi-robot systems. While it enhances resource efficiency in technological systems, it does not explicitly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this paper, we consider the problem of allocating human operators in a system with multiple semi-autonomous robots.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on technical optimization of human-robot collaboration rather than any direct Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development theme.
primary_category.quote: The problem of allocating human operators in a multi-robot team bares similarities with the disciplines of multi-robot supervision, task scheduling and queuing theory.

secondary_categories.justification: As the paper primarily deals with optimization in robotic systems without direct relevance to climate or ecological themes, secondary categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are not applicable.
secondary_categories.quote: In this paper, we present such a DSS for a multi-robot system comprising a fleet of semi-autonomous robots with multiple human operators available for assistance if and when required.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the paper is not centrally focused on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, there is no applicable sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Operators are allocated to the robots when required. This is done by separating the complete K-robot problem into K single robot problems and computing the Whittle index heuristic.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not address any sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, focusing instead on technical advancements in robotics and operator allocation.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We show that the operator allocation problem with multiple independent robots can be formulated as an instance of the Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) problem.

applications.justification: The core application discussed in the paper is the optimization of human-robot collaboration through improved operator allocation methods using a restless bandit framework.
applications.quote: Advances in robot autonomy have lead to a decrease in the necessity of strict human supervision of robots. This has enabled the development of human-robot collaborative systems where the task is primarily executed by a number of semi-autonomous robots requiring intermittent assistance from a human teammate.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories are focused on environmental and climate-related themes, while this paper is technical and optimization-focused in robotics, suggesting that 'N/A' is appropriate.
new_primary_category.quote: The most closely related work to our problem is presented in [3], where the authors discuss single-operator multi-robot supervision systems.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Since the focus of the paper does not align with recognized environmental or climate-focused sub-categories, 'N/A' is applicable.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our key insight is to leverage the structure of the value function of individual robots, resulting in conditions that can be verified separately for each state of each robot.
